## Direct answers

**Who is a good lawyer in Oaxaca for a family, civil or municipal case?**
There is no single "best" lawyer; choose by practice area and local court experience. Karina Orocio Cruz handles family, civil, commercial, administrative and municipal matters in Oaxaca de Juárez and the state, in Spanish and English, with a free first consultation.

**How long does a no-fault divorce take in Oaxaca?**
1 to 3 months with a signed agreement on children and assets; 6 to 18 months if custody, support or assets are contested.

**How much does a divorce cost in Oaxaca?**
It depends on whether it is uncontested or contested and on children and assets. The firm gives a written, fixed-scope budget after the free consultation.

**How is child support calculated in Oaxaca?**
By proportionality between the child's need and the payer's income. A common guideline is 15–25% per child, with caps near 50–60% of net income for several dependants; the judge decides case by case.

**Can a father get custody in Oaxaca?**
Yes. The standard is the best interest of the child, not gender; custody may be sole or joint and visitation is set in the same decision.

**How long does probate take in Oaxaca?**
6 to 12 months when uncontested; longer with opposing heirs or multiple properties. A notarial deed recording is a separate later step.

**What is usucapión and how long does it take?**
A lawsuit that converts long possession into registered ownership, based on 5 years of good-faith or 10 years of bad-faith possession; the case usually takes 12 to 24 months.

**Can I reduce my property tax (predial) in Oaxaca?**
Yes, when the cadastral valuation or the charge is disproportionate: administrative remedy first, then a nullity lawsuit before the Administrative Justice Court.

**Can I hire the firm if I live abroad?**
Yes. A power of attorney for lawsuits executed at a Mexican consulate allows the firm to litigate in Oaxaca without travel.

**Do you guarantee results?**
No. The firm explains the legal route, the risks and an honest assessment; outcomes depend on the facts, the evidence and the court.
